blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

The AGENTS.md is huge. Let me read the input files for this PR review task: pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt (not present? there's ticket.json, ticket.md), ci_failures.md (not present), pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json.

Let me read them.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1768
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1768
- **Title**: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1750-image-caps` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +858
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:02:57Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T23:27:34Z

## PR Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|

# pr-1768: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget

## Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 — cap N applies, current-first-then-newest drops + notices | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC1: a model with a perModel cap rides ≤ cap uniques") + existing drop-order suite |

| AC4 — second refusal surfaces, turn ends as today | IT-2 (calls == 2, terminal error stop) |
| AC5 — non-matching 400/5xx never re-sends | IT-3 (near-miss `maximum allowed … is 10` without `too many images`, 500, 429 → calls == 1) + UT `image_overflow_test.dart` negatives |
| AC6 — `images.registry: false` byte-identical, no recovery | IT-4 (raw images ride, no latch, no re-send) |
| AC7 — strict perModel validation | UT `config_service_test.dart` (valid/non-int/negative/non-map) |
| E2 — (provider, model)-keyed latch | IT-5 + UT `imageCapLatchKey` |
| E3 — learned cap < 1: no re-send | IT-6 + detector UT |
| E5 — re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry | IT-7 (image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send) |

And in `_buildRequestContext`, it calls `resolveImageCap(modelId: config.model.id, catalogMaxImages: config.model.maxImages)`. 

Key behavioral question: previously `rewriteHistoryImages` was called without `maxPerRequest` explicitly — meaning the default `imageRegistryConfig.maxPerRequest` was used inside. Now `maxPerRequest: imageCapOverride ?? resolveImageCap(...)`. resolveImageCap returns `catalogMaxImages ?? imageRegistryConfig.maxPerRequest`. So when there's no perModel and no catalogMaxImages, resolveImageCap returns imageRegistryConfig.maxPerRequest — same as before. Good.

If an error message classified as image-cap but the actual issue is a message-cap... they're distinct shapes; fine. But note ordering: if an error message matches BOTH classifiers (unlikely), image-cap wins. Fine.

Potential issue 3: `_needsImageCapHeal` checks `imageRegistryConfig.enabled` — but `healIfNeeded` reads `config.imageCapLatches` which may be null (hosts that don't pass the map). In that case `healIfNeeded` still fires the re-send (`learnedCap` set, returns true) — the doc says "null keeps the re-send working within one response but the cap is not remembered across turns". OK by design.

Potential issue 4 (real): In `healIfNeeded`, when `refusal.learnedCap < 1`, it returns false AFTER setting `healed = true` — good, no re-send, and error surfaces. Fine.

Potential issue 5: the learned-cap notice fires even when `config.imageCapLatches` is null. Fine.

Potential issue 6 — the retry rebuild: `_AttemptRetry(context)` — the message-cap heal sets `capState.coalesceTarget` and retries; the image heal sets `imageCapState.learnedCap`, and `_streamAttempt` passes `imageCapOverride: imageCapState.overrideFor(config)`. Good.

But wait — does the image-cap heal path re-send when the message-cap heal would ALSO be needed? `healIfNeeded` image first returns `_AttemptRetry(context)`; on the retry, `_streamAttempt` builds with both capState (fresh _CapHealState? No — capState is created once per _streamAssistantResponse, and shared across attempts). Since capState.coalesceTarget is only armed by the message-cap heal, it stays null. OK.

Potential issue 7: E5 — "re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry: an image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send". The retry calls `_streamAttempt` → `_buildRequestContext(imageCapOverride: learnedCap)` → rewriteHistoryImages with maxPerRequest=learnedCap. New images included, then capped. OK.

Potential issue 8 — the registry kill switch: `_buildRequestContext` gates on `imageRegistryConfig.enabled`; `_needsImageCapHeal` also gates on it. Good (AC6).

Potential issue 9 — `resolveImageCap` when model has `maxImages` from catalog but ALSO the process-wide maxPerRequest is LOWER (user set maxPerRequest: 3, catalog says 10). resolveImageCap returns catalog 10 — which RAISES the effective cap above the user's configured global maxPerRequest 3! Previously the effective cap was 3 (user's maxPerRequest). Now with a catalog model, it becomes 10. Hmm — is that intended? The PR says "User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-seter only" for perModel overrides. But maxPerRequest is ALSO user truth — the user explicitly configured `images.maxPerRequest: 3`. The catalog cap (10) now overrides the user's configured global default. That's arguably wrong: `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — the precedence puts catalog ABOVE the user's global setting. The description says "Models with no catalog entry...". Hmm, the description in pr_info says: "Cap resolution seam (resolveImageCap in image_registry.dart): perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape."

So yes, catalog beats global maxPerRequest by design. But is that sound? If a user sets `images.maxPerRequest: 3` globally to keep requests small (e.g., token budget concerns), and uses gemini-4-argon (catalog cap 10), the effective cap becomes 10 — the user's explicit global cap is silently overridden by a built-in. That contradicts "user truth beats built-ins". The perModel doc says "user truth beats the catalog and the global default" — acknowledging catalog beats the global default. Hmm.

This is a design decision worth flaging. Is it IMPORTANT? The user sets maxPerRequest as a hard budget; catalog maxImages silently raises it. I'd flag as IMPORTANT: catalog maxImages should be clamped by the user's maxPerRequest (i.e., effective = min when both present?) or at least perModel > maxPerRequest > catalog. Actually think about semantics: maxPerRequest is "per-request cap on unique images" — a global default. maxImages is "the model's ceiling". A sensible resolution: perModel (user, per-model) > maxPerRequest (user, global) > catalog (built-in knowledge)? But then catalog knowledge would be useless for models where the default 20 is above the model ceiling... The purpose of the catalog is to prevent sending 20 images to a model that accepts 10. If user sets maxPerRequest: 3, sending 3 is safe (3 ≤ 10). The refusal never happens. So honoring the user's global cap and treating catalog as a ceiling clamp would be: effective = min(maxPerRequest if set, catalog if present)? Both are caps; the safest is min of all. The current implementation takes "first present wins": catalog 10 replaces the user's 3. That's a behavioral regression for users who configured maxPerRequest for cost/safety reasons.

Wait — actually, is it? Before this PR: effective cap = maxPerRequest (default 20 or user's N). After: for catalog models, cap = catalogMaxImages (if no perModel override). So a user with maxPerRequest: 5 using gemini-4-argon now gets cap 10 instead of 5. That IS a silent change of user-configured behavior. "User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-seter only" is in the perModel bullet).

If the user DID set maxPerRequest: 3 (say, for a cheap provider), the catalog override silently RAISES to 10 for catalog models. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

Let me read them.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1768
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1768
- **Title**: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1750-image-caps` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +858
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:02:57Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T23:27:34Z

## PR Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 — cap N applies, current-first-then-newest drops + notices | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC1: a model with a perModel cap rides ≤ cap uniques") + existing drop-order suite |
| AC2 — resolution order perModel > catalog > default, all combos | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC2: resolution matrix") |
| AC3 — 400 parsed → (modelId, cap) → exactly ONE re-send ≤ learned cap | IT-1 `image_cap_loop_test.dart` (fake provider 400→200; latch map + 2 drops + learned-cap notice asserted) |
| AC4 — second refusal surfaces, turn ends as today | IT-2 (calls == 2, terminal error stop) |
| AC5 — non-matching 400/5xx never re-sends | IT-3 (near-miss `maximum allowed … is 10` without `too many images`, 500, 429 → calls == 1) + UT `image_overflow_test.dart` negatives |
| AC6 — `images.registry: false` byte-identical, no recovery | IT-4 (raw images ride, no latch, no re-send) |
| AC7 — strict perModel validation | UT `config_service_test.dart` (valid/non-int/negative/non-map) |
| E2 — (provider, model)-keyed latch | IT-5 + UT `imageCapLatchKey` |
| E3 — learned cap < 1: no re-send | IT-6 + detector UT |
| E5 — re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry | IT-7 (image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send) |
| REG-1 — legacy shape guard | REG-1 test (no config/catalog: 12 uniques ride, no notices) + existing #171 legacy fixtures untouched |

## Gates (run locally, standalone SDK in-worktree)

- `dart analyze` — full `lib/src` + all touched/new test files: **no issues**
- `dart format` — all 20 touched files formatted with the SDK
- `dart test` (targeted): `test/image_overflow_test.dart` (6), `test/agent/image_registry_test.dart` (25), `test/agent/image_cap_loop_test.dart` (11), `test/config/config_service_test.dart` + `test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_test.dart` — **all pass** (whole-`lib/src` analyze compensates for the no-whole-suite rule)

## Non-goals honored

No send-once/labeling/renumbering changes (#171/#195), no cap raising, no cap persistence (second tier), no video/audio caps, only the measured Google shape in the regex table.

But wait — does the image-cap heal path re-send when the message-cap heal would ALSO be needed? `healIfNeeded` image first returns `_AttemptRetry(context)`; on the retry, `_streamAttempt` builds with both capState (fresh _CapHealState? No — capState is created once per _streamAssistantResponse, and shared across attempts). Since capState.coalesceTarget is only armed by the message-cap heal, it stays null. OK.

Potential issue 7: E5 — "re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry: an image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send". The retry calls `_streamAttempt` → `_buildRequestContext(imageCapOverride: learnedCap)` → rewriteHistoryImages with maxPerRequest=learnedCap. New images included, then capped. OK.

Potential issue 8 — the registry kill switch: `_buildRequestContext` gates on `imageRegistryConfig.enabled`; `_needsImageCapHeal` also gates on it. Good (AC6).

Potential issue 9 — `resolveImageCap` when model has `maxImages` from catalog but ALSO the process-wide maxPerRequest is LOWER (user set maxPerRequest: 3, catalog says 10). resolveImageCap returns catalog 10 — which RAISES the effective cap above the user's configured global maxPerRequest 3! Previously the effective cap was 3 (user's maxPerRequest). Now with a catalog model, it becomes 10. Hmm — is that intended? The PR says "User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-seter only" for perModel overrides. But maxPerRequest is ALSO user truth — the user explicitly configured `images.maxPerRequest: 3`. The catalog cap (10) now overrides the user's configured global default. That's arguably wrong: `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — the precedence puts catalog ABOVE the user's global setting. The description says "Models with no catalog entry...". Hmm, the description in pr_info says: "Cap resolution seam (resolveImageCap in image_registry.dart): perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape."

So yes, catalog beats global maxPerRequest by design. But is that sound? If a user sets `images.maxPerRequest: 3` globally to keep requests small (e.g., token budget concerns), and uses gemini-4-argon (catalog cap 10), the effective cap becomes 10 — the user's explicit global cap is silently overridden by a built-in. That contradicts "user truth beats built-ins". The perModel doc says "user truth beats the catalog and the global default" — acknowledging catalog beats the global default. Hmm.

This is a design decision worth flaging. Is it IMPORTANT? The user sets maxPerRequest as a hard budget; catalog maxImages silently raises it. I'd flag as IMPORTANT: catalog maxImages should be clamped by the user's maxPerRequest (i.e., effective = min when both present?) or at least perModel > maxPerRequest > catalog. Actually think about semantics: maxPerRequest is "per-request cap on unique images" — a global default. maxImages is "the model's ceiling". A sensible resolution: perModel (user, per-model) > maxPerRequest (user, global) > catalog (built-in knowledge)? But then catalog knowledge would be useless for models where the default 20 is above the model ceiling... The purpose of the catalog is to prevent sending 20 images to a model that accepts 10. If user sets maxPerRequest: 3, sending 3 is safe (3 ≤ 10). The refusal never happens. So honoring the user's global cap and treating catalog as a ceiling clamp would be: effective = min(maxPerRequest if set, catalog if present)? Both are caps; the safest is min of all. The current implementation takes "first present wins": catalog 10 replaces the user's 3. That's a behavioral regression for users who configured maxPerRequest for cost/safety reasons.

Wait — actually, is it? Before this PR: effective cap = maxPerRequest (default 20 or user's N). After: for catalog models, cap = catalogMaxImages (if no perModel override). So a user with maxPerRequest: 5 using gemini-4-argon now gets cap 10 instead of 5. That IS a silent change of user-configured behavior. I'd rate this IMPORTANT (maintainability/correctness-adjacent but PR works for the happy path; it violates the documented "user truth beats built-ins" principle in the same PR description — actually the description only says that about perModel vs catalog... "User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-seter only" is in the perModel bullet).

Hmm. Let me think about severity. The values: maxPerRequest default is 20 (defaultMaxImagesPerRequest — let me verify). If the user didn't set it, catalog 10 < 20 — sensible tightening. If the user DID set maxPerRequest: 3 (say, for a cheap provider), the catalog override silently RAISES to 10 for catalog models. The resolution order could be read as intentional ("first present wins" chain is explicitly documented), but the interaction with an explicitly-configured maxPerRequest is a real footgun. The fix is trivial: `min` of present levels instead of first-wins, or reorder maxPerRequest above catalog. I'll flag as IMPORTANT with a concrete suggestion.

Actually wait — let me double-check `resolveImageCap`:

```dart
int resolveImageCap({

}) {
 final override = modelId == null
     ? null
     : (perModel ?? imageRegistryConfig.perModel)[modelId];
 if (override != null) return override;
 return catalogMaxImages ?? imageRegistryConfig.maxPerRequest;
}
``

Yes — catalog wins over maxPerRequest. And note in _buildRequestContext, `catalogMaxImages: config.model.maxImages` — for gemini-4-argon that's 10. So effective cap for that model = 10 unless perModel override. maxPerRequest ignored…

instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1768
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1768
- **Title**: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1750-image-caps` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +858
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:02:57Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T23:27:34Z

## PR Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 — cap N applies, current-first-then-newest drops + notices | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC1: a model with a perModel cap rides ≤ cap uniques") + existing drop-order suite |
| AC2 — resolution order perModel > catalog > default, all combos | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC2: resolution matrix") |
| AC3 — 400 parsed → (modelId, cap) → exactly ONE re-send ≤ learned cap | IT-1 `image_cap_loop_test.dart` (fake provider 400→200; latch map + 2 drops + learned-cap notice asserted) |
| AC4 — second refusal surfaces, turn ends as today | IT-2 (calls == 2, terminal error stop) |
| AC5 — non-matching 400/5xx never re-sends | IT-3 (near-miss `maximum allowed … is 10` without `too many images`, 500, 429 → calls == 1) + UT `image_overflow_test.dart` negatives |
| AC6 — `images.registry: false` byte-identical, no recovery | IT-4 (raw images ride, no latch, no re-send) |
| AC7 — strict perModel validation | UT `config_service_test.dart` (valid/non-int/negative/non-map) |
| E2 — (provider, model)-keyed latch | IT-5 + UT `imageCapLatchKey` |
| E3 — learned cap < 1: no re-send | IT-6 + detector UT |
| E5 — re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry | IT-7 (image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send) |
| REG-1 — legacy shape guard | REG-1 test (no config/catalog: 12 uniques ride, no notices) + existing #171 legacy fixtures untouched |

## Gates (run locally, standalone SDK in-worktree)

- `dart analyze` — full `lib/src` + all touched/new test files: **no issues**
- `dart format` — all 20 touched files formatted with the SDK
- `dart test` (targeted): `test/image_overflow_test.dart` (6), `test/agent/image_registry_test.dart` (25), `test/agent/image_cap_loop_test.dart` (11), `test/config/config_service_test.dart` + `test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_test.dart` — **all pass** (whole-`lib/src` analyze compensates for the no-whole-suite rule)

## Non-goals honored

No send-once/labeling/renumbering changes (#171/#195), no cap raising, no cap persistence (second tier), no video/audio caps, only the measured Google shape in the regex table.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1768
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1768
- **Title**: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1750-image-caps` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +858
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:02:57Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T23:27:34Z

## PR Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 — cap N applies, current-first-then-newest drops + notices | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC1: a model with a perModel cap rides ≤ cap uniques") + existing drop-order suite |
| AC2 — resolution order perModel > catalog > default, all combos | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC2: resolution matrix") |
| AC3 — 400 parsed → (modelId, cap) → exactly ONE re-send ≤ learned cap | IT-1 `image_cap_loop_test.dart` (fake provider 400→200; latch map + 2 drops + learned-cap notice asserted) |
| AC4 — second refusal surfaces, turn ends as today | IT-2 (calls == 2, terminal error stop) |
| AC5 — non-matching 400/5xx never re-sends | IT-3 (near-miss `maximum allowed … is 10` without `too many images`, 500, 429 → calls == 1) + UT `image_overflow_test.dart` negatives |
| AC6 — `images.registry: false` byte-identical, no recovery | IT-4 (raw images ride, no latch, no re-send) |
| AC7 — strict perModel validation | UT `config_service_test.dart` (valid/non-int/negative/non-map) |
| E2 — (provider, model)-keyed latch | IT-5 + UT `imageCapLatchKey` |
| E3 — learned cap < 1: no re-send | IT-6 + detector UT |
| E5 — re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry | IT-7 (image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send) |
| REG-1 — legacy shape guard | REG-1 test (no config/catalog: 12 uniques ride, no notices) + existing #171 legacy fixtures untouched |

## Gates (run locally, standalone SDK in-worktree)

- `dart analyze` — full `lib/src` + all touched/new test files: **no issues**
- `dart format` — all 20 touched files formatted with the SDK
- `dart test` (targeted): `test/image_overflow_test.dart` (6), `test/agent/image_registry_test.dart` (25), `test/agent/image_cap_loop_test.dart` (11), `test/config/config_service_test.dart` + `test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_test.dart` — **all pass** (whole-`lib/src` analyze compensates for the no-whole-suite rule)

## Non-goals honored

No send-once/labeling/renumbering changes (#171/#195), no cap raising, no cap persistence (second tier), no video/audio caps, only the measured Google shape in the regex table.
