# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1768._

> ℹ️ **3 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `CHANGELOG.md` line 27

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
🚨 **BLOCKING: merge conflict with `main` (CHANGELOG.md)**

The branch predates main's gh-1757 merge (#1764, `823395d`) and both sides append to the `## Unreleased` section, so the merge is broken. Verified against live `origin/main`:

```
$ git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in CHANGELOG.md   (exit 1)
```

The factory bot flagged the same conflict. Please rebase onto `main` and keep both entries under `## Unreleased` (main's entries read newest-first, so `feat(#1750)` slots in below `- fix(gh-1757)`). Validation re-runs automatically after the push.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart` line 285

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the app host never sees the learned-cap notice**

`_wireImageCapLearnedNotice()` is wired in the CLI only (`agent_cli_io.dart`). The Flutter app wires every other "never silent" notice through `AppLog.i` — `_wireImageDropNotice` (F4), `_wireOperativePinNotice` (gh-1409), the text-only drops (#638) in `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart` — but nothing sets `imageCapLearnedNotice` there. In the desktop app an adaptive re-send therefore logs the per-image drop lines with no "provider refused / cap learned" context line, which is exactly the confusion the notice exists to prevent.

Mirror the pattern in `AgentService` (an `AppLog.i('images', 'provider refused: too many images for $modelId — cap learned: $cap; re-sending with fewer images')` from a `_wireImageCapLearnedNotice` next to `_wireImageDropNotice`) so both hosts tell the same story.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart` line 289

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: provider-controlled text interpolated into the terminal line**

`modelId` here is regex-extracted from the raw provider error body (`classifyImageCapError`, group `(.+?)`) — a buggy or hostile endpoint can embed ANSI escape sequences or control characters that ride verbatim into this `io.writeln` and scramble the transcript. The same trust surface already exists for `errorMessage` rendering, so this is hardening, not a new hole: consider stripping control chars from `refusal.modelId` (e.g. `replaceAll(RegExp(r'[\x00-\x1f\x7f]'), '')`) before interpolation — one line, and the fa.log entry benefits too.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` line 1385

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

Tests look reasonable. Note the AC2 matrix: "perModel absent, catalog present → 10" — the catalog-over-global-default precedence is asserted intentionally. The question of a USER-SET maxPerRequest being overridden by the catalog remains: in the matrix they set `imageRegistryConfig = ImageRegistryConfig(maxPerRequest: 20)` (the default, not user-set) and `resolve(modelId: 'm', catalog: 10)` → 10. So the design intentionally puts catalog above the global default. But when the USER explicitly sets `maxPerRequest: 3`, the catalog still overrides it to 10. There's no way to distinguish "user-set" from "default 20" in the current ImageRegistryConfig (both are just `maxPerRequest: 3` vs default). So user's explicit global cap IS overridden by catalog for catalog models. That's the finding. Severity: the default is 20 and catalog values are measured provider ceilings; the only case where it bites is a user lowering maxPerRequest for token/cost reasons. It contradicts the PR's own "user truth beats built-ins" claim (stated for perModel). I'll flag as IMPORTANT.

Hmm, wait. Let me re-read the PR description: "`images.perModel.<modelId>` config override — ... User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-seter only." And the ImageRegistryConfig.perModel doc: "user truth beats the catalog and the global default". So the author DID think about precedence: perModel (user, per-model) > catalog (built-in, per-model) > maxPerRequest (user global default... or built-in default). The precedence treats maxPerRequest as the lowest layer. Arguably `maxPerRequest` is a GLOBAL default while catalog maxImages is MODEL-SPECIFIC knowledge — more specific wins. That's a defensible reading: model-specific > global. But it's still a silent behavior change for users who set maxPerRequest explicitly for budget reasons: with a catalog model their cap goes UP without notice. Pre-PR, cap was maxPerRequest always.

Practical risk: low-medium. A user who set maxPerRequest: 3 to save tokens now sends 10 images to gemini-4-argon — more cost. No refusal (10 ≤ real cap). It's a real, silent precedence surprise worth an IMPORTANT. I'll phrase it as a question-grade IMPORTANT with a concrete fix: honor an explicitly-configured maxPerRequest as a hard ceiling too (min of catalog and maxPerRequest), or document that maxPerRequest no longer caps catalog models. Since ImageRegistryConfig can't distinguish explicit vs default... actually it can: default ctor uses `defaultMaxImagesPerRequest`; if user sets it, parseImagesSection returns a config with maxPerRequest set. But `ImageRegistryConfig()` default also has maxPerRequest = 20. Hosts publish `parseImagesSection(...) ?? const ImageRegistryConfig()` — indistinguishable. The clean fix: make maxPerRequest nullable internally (null = default) and resolve `min` where both present. That's a design change; as a reviewer I'll raise it as IMPORTANT and let the author decide.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1768
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1768
- **Title**: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1750-image-caps` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +858
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:02:57Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T23:27:34Z

## PR Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 — cap N applies, current-first-then-newest drops + notices | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC1: a model with a perModel cap rides ≤ cap uniques") + existing drop-order suite |
| AC2 — resolution order perModel > catalog > default, all combos | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC2: resolution matrix") |
| AC3 — 400 parsed → (modelId, cap) → exactly ONE re-send ≤ learned cap | IT-1 `image_cap_loop_test.dart` (fake provider 400→200; latch map + 2 drops + learned-cap notice asserted) |
| AC4 — second refusal surfaces, turn ends as today | IT-2 (calls == 2, terminal error stop) |
| AC5 — non-matching 400/5xx never re-sends | IT-3 (near-miss `maximum allowed … is 10` without `too many images`, 500, 429 → calls == 1) + UT `image_overflow_test.dart` negatives |
| AC6 — `images.registry: false` byte-identical, no recovery | IT-4 (raw images ride, no latch, no re-send) |
| AC7 — strict perModel validation | UT `config_service_test.dart` (valid/non-int/negative/non-map) |
| E2 — (provider, model)-keyed latch | IT-5 + UT `imageCapLatchKey` |
| E3 — learned cap < 1: no re-send | IT-6 + detector UT |
| E5 — re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry | IT-7 (image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send) |
| REG-1 — legacy shape guard | REG-1 test (no config/catalog: 12 uniques ride, no notices) + existing #171 legacy fixtures untouched |

## Gates (run locally, standalone SDK in-worktree)

- `dart analyze` — full `lib/src` + all touched/new test files: **no issues**
- `dart format` — all 20 touched files formatted with the SDK
- `dart test` (targeted): `test/image_overflow_test.dart` (6), `test/agent/image_registry_test.dart` (25), `test/agent/image_cap_loop_test.dart` (11), `test/config/config_service_test.dart` + `test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_test.dart` — **all pass** (whole-`lib/src` analyze compensates for the no-whole-suite rule)

## Non-goals honored

No send-once/labeling/renumbering changes (#171/#195), no cap raising, no cap persistence (second tier), no video/audio caps, only the measured Google shape in the regex table.

# PR Discussion History

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
🚨 **BLOCKING: merge conflict with `main` (CHANGELOG.md)**

The branch predates main's gh-1757 merge (#1764, `823395d`) and both sides append to the `## Unreleased` section, so the merge is broken. Verified against live `origin/main`:

```
$ git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in CHANGELOG.md   (exit 1)
```

The factory bot flagged the same conflict. Please rebase onto `main` and keep both entries under `## Unreleased` (main's entries read newest-first, so `feat(#1750)` slots in below `- fix(gh-1757)`). Validation re-runs automatically after the push.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart` line 285

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the app host never sees the learned-cap notice**

`_wireImageCapLearnedNotice()` is wired in the CLI only (`agent_cli_io.dart`). The Flutter app wires every other "never silent" notice through `AppLog.i` — `_wireImageDropNotice` (F4), `_wireOperativePinNotice` (gh-1409), the text-only drops (#638) in `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart` — but nothing sets `imageCapLearnedNotice` there. In the desktop app an adaptive re-send therefore logs the per-image drop lines with no "provider refused / cap learned" context line, which is exactly the confusion the notice exists to prevent.

Mirror the pattern in `AgentService` (an `AppLog.i('images', 'provider refused: too many images for $modelId — cap learned: $cap; re-sending with fewer images')` from a `_wireImageCapLearnedNotice` next to `_wireImageDropNotice`) so both hosts tell the same story.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart` line 289

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: provider-controlled text interpolated into the terminal line**

`modelId` here is regex-extracted from the raw provider error body (`classifyImageCapError`, group `(.+?)`) — a buggy or hostile endpoint can embed ANSI escape sequences or control characters that ride verbatim into this `io.writeln` and scramble the transcript. The same trust surface already exists for `errorMessage` rendering, so this is hardening, not a new hole: consider stripping control chars from `refusal.modelId` (e.g. `replaceAll(RegExp(r'[\x00-\x1f\x7f]'), '')`) before interpolation — one line, and the fa.log entry benefits too.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` line 1385

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: perModel validation now lives in two hand-synced copies**

The strict rules (must be a `YamlMap`; every value a positive `int` naming the offending key) are implemented twice — here in the boot validator and again in `parseImagesSection`'s `readPerModelCap`/`readPerModel` (`cli_config.dart`). This extends the pre-existing `maxPerRequest` duplication, so it follows the local pattern, but the two copies must now drift in lockstep (messages are asserted by tests on both sides). When the third `images:` key arrives, consider extracting one shared validator both paths call so the strict schema has a single source of truth.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` line 440

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `agent_loop.dart` is at 97.6% of the 2800-line loc gate**

Tests look reasonable. Note the AC2 matrix: "perModel absent, catalog present → 10" — the catalog-over-global-default precedence is asserted intentionally. The question of a USER-SET maxPerRequest being overridden by the catalog remains: in the matrix they set `imageRegistryConfig = ImageRegistryConfig(maxPerRequest: 20)` (the default, not user-set) and `resolve(modelId: 'm', catalog: 10)` → 10. So the design intentionally puts catalog above the global default. But when the USER explicitly sets `maxPerRequest: 3`, the catalog still overrides it to 10. There's no way to distinguish "user-set" from "default 20" in the current ImageRegistryConfig (both are just `maxPerRequest: 3` vs default). So user's explicit global cap IS overridden by catalog for catalog models. That's the finding. Severity: the default is 20 and catalog values are measured provider ceilings; the only case where it bites is a user lowering maxPerRequest for token/cost reasons. It contradicts the PR's own "user truth beats built-ins" claim (stated for perModel). I'll flag as IMPORTANT.

Hmm, wait. Let me re-read the PR description: "`images.perModel.<modelId>` config override — ... User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-seter only." And the ImageRegistryConfig.perModel doc: "user truth beats the catalog and the global default". So the author DID think about precedence: perModel (user, per-model) > catalog (built-in, per-model) > maxPerRequest (user global default... or built-in default). The precedence treats maxPerRequest as the lowest layer. Arguably `maxPerRequest` is a GLOBAL default while catalog maxImages is MODEL-SPECIFIC knowledge — more specific wins. That's a defensible reading: model-specific > global. But it's still a silent behavior change for users who set maxPerRequest explicitly for budget reasons: with a catalog model their cap goes UP without notice. Pre-PR, cap was maxPerRequest always.

Practical risk: low-medium. A user who set maxPerRequest: 3 to save tokens now sends 10 images to gemini-4-argon — more cost. No refusal (10 ≤ real cap). It's a real, silent precedence surprise worth an IMPORTANT. I'll phrase it as a question-grade IMPORTANT with a concrete fix: honor an explicitly-configured maxPerRequest as a hard ceiling too (min of catalog and maxPerRequest), or document that maxPerRequest no longer caps catalog models. Since ImageRegistryConfig can't distinguish explicit vs default... actually it can: default ctor uses `defaultMaxImagesPerRequest`; if user sets it, parseImagesSection returns a config with maxPerRequest set. But `ImageRegistryConfig()` default also has maxPerRequest = 20. Hosts publish `parseImagesSection(...) ?? const ImageRegistryConfig()` — indistinguishable. The clean fix: make maxPerRequest nullable internally (null = default) and resolve `min` where both present. That's a design change; as a reviewer I'll raise it as IMPORTANT and let the author decide.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1768
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1768
- **Title**: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1750-image-caps` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +858
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:02:57Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T23:27:34Z

## PR Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 — cap N applies, current-first-then-newest drops + notices | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC1: a model with a perModel cap rides ≤ cap uniques") + existing drop-order suite |
| AC2 — resolution order perModel > catalog > default, all combos | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC2: resolution matrix") |
| AC3 — 400 parsed → (modelId, cap) → exactly ONE re-send ≤ learned cap | IT-1 `image_cap_loop_test.dart` (fake provider 400→200; latch map + 2 drops + learned-cap notice asserted) |
| AC4 — second refusal surfaces, turn ends as today | IT-2 (calls == 2, terminal error stop) |
| AC5 — non-matching 400/5xx never re-sends | IT-3 (near-miss `maximum allowed … is 10` without `too many images`, 500, 429 → calls == 1) + UT `image_overflow_test.dart` negatives |
| AC6 — `images.registry: false` byte-identical, no recovery | IT-4 (raw images ride, no latch, no re-send) |
| AC7 — strict perModel validation | UT `config_service_test.dart` (valid/non-int/negative/non-map) |
| E2 — (provider, model)-keyed latch | IT-5 + UT `imageCapLatchKey` |
| E3 — learned cap < 1: no re-send | IT-6 + detector UT |
| E5 — re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry | IT-7 (image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send) |
| REG-1 — legacy shape guard | REG-1 test (no config/catalog: 12 uniques ride, no notices) + existing #171 legacy fixtures untouched |

## Gates (run locally, standalone SDK in-worktree)

- `dart analyze` — full `lib/src` + all touched/new test files: **no issues**
- `dart format` — all 20 touched files formatted with the SDK
- `dart test` (targeted): `test/image_overflow_test.dart` (6), `test/agent/image_registry_test.dart` (25), `test/agent/image_cap_loop_test.dart` (11), `test/config/config_service_test.dart` + `test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_test.dart` — **all pass** (whole-`lib/src` analyze compensates for the no-whole-suite rule)

## Non-goals honored

No send-once/labeling/renumbering changes (#171/#195), no cap raising, no cap persistence (second tier), no video/audio caps, only the measured Google shape in the regex table.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1768._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `CHANGELOG.md` line 27

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
🚨 **BLOCKING: merge conflict with `main` (CHANGELOG.md)**

The branch predates main's gh-1757 merge (#1764, `823395d`) and both sides append to the `## Unreleased` section, so the merge is broken. Verified against live `origin/main`:

```
$ git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in CHANGELOG.md   (exit 1)
```

The factory bot flagged the same conflict. Please rebase onto `main` and keep both entries under `## Unreleased` (main's entries read newest-first, so `feat(#1750)` slots in below `- fix(gh-1757)`). Validation re-runs automatically after the push.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart` line 285

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the app host never sees the learned-cap notice**

`_wireImageCapLearnedNotice()` is wired in the CLI only (`agent_cli_io.dart`). The Flutter app wires every other "never silent" notice through `AppLog.i` — `_wireImageDropNotice` (F4), `_wireOperativePinNotice` (gh-1409), the text-only drops (#638) in `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart` — but nothing sets `imageCapLearnedNotice` there. In the desktop app an adaptive re-send therefore logs the per-image drop lines with no "provider refused / cap learned" context line, which is exactly the confusion the notice exists to prevent.

Mirror the pattern in `AgentService` (an `AppLog.i('images', 'provider refused: too many images for $modelId — cap learned: $cap; re-sending with fewer images')` from a `_wireImageCapLearnedNotice` next to `_wireImageDropNotice`) so both hosts tell the same story.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart` line 289

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: provider-controlled text interpolated into the terminal line**

`modelId` here is regex-extracted from the raw provider error body (`classifyImageCapError`, group `(.+?)`) — a buggy or hostile endpoint can embed ANSI escape sequences or control characters that ride verbatim into this `io.writeln` and scramble the transcript. The same trust surface already exists for `errorMessage` rendering, so this is hardening, not a new hole: consider stripping control chars from `refusal.modelId` (e.g. `replaceAll(RegExp(r'[\x00-\x1f\x7f]'), '')`) before interpolation — one line, and the fa.log entry benefits too.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` line 1385

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: perModel validation now lives in two hand-synced copies**

The strict rules (must be a `YamlMap`; every value a positive `int` naming the offending key) are implemented twice — here in the boot validator and again in `parseImagesSection`'s `readPerModelCap`/`readPerModel` (`cli_config.dart`). This extends the pre-existing `maxPerRequest` duplication, so it follows the local pattern, but the two copies must now drift in lockstep (messages are asserted by tests on both sides). When the third `images:` key arrives, consider extracting one shared validator both paths call so the strict schema has a single source of truth.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` line 440

Tests look reasonable. Note the AC2 matrix: "perModel absent, catalog present → 10" — the catalog-over-global-default precedence is asserted intentionally. The question of a USER-SET maxPerRequest being overridden by the catalog remains: in the matrix they set `imageRegistryConfig = ImageRegistryConfig(maxPerRequest: 20)` (the default, not user-set) and `resolve(modelId: 'm', catalog: 10)` → 10. So the design intentionally puts catalog above the global default. But when the USER explicitly sets `maxPerRequest: 3`, the catalog still overrides it to 10. There's no way to distinguish "user-set" from "default 20" in the current ImageRegistryConfig (both are just `maxPerRequest: 3` vs default). So user's explicit global cap IS overridden by catalog for catalog models. That's the finding. Severity: the default is 20 and catalog values are measured provider ceilings; the only case where it bites is a user lowering maxPerRequest for token/cost reasons. It contradicts the PR's own "user truth beats built-ins" claim (stated for perModel). I'll flag as IMPORTANT.

Hmm, wait. Let me re-read the PR description: "`images.perModel.<modelId>` config override — ... User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-seter only." And the ImageRegistryConfig.perModel doc: "user truth beats the catalog and the global default". So the author DID think about precedence: perModel (user, per-model) > catalog (built-in, per-model) > maxPerRequest (user global default... or built-in default). The precedence treats maxPerRequest as the lowest layer. Arguably `maxPerRequest` is a GLOBAL default while catalog maxImages is MODEL-SPECIFIC knowledge — more specific wins. That's a defensible reading: model-specific > global. But it's still a silent behavior change for users who set maxPerRequest explicitly for budget reasons: with a catalog model their cap goes UP without notice. Pre-PR, cap was maxPerRequest always.

Practical risk: low-medium. A user who set maxPerRequest: 3 to save tokens now sends 10 images to gemini-4-argon — more cost. No refusal (10 ≤ real cap). It's a real, silent precedence surprise worth an IMPORTANT. I'll phrase it as a question-grade IMPORTANT with a concrete fix: honor an explicitly-configured maxPerRequest as a hard ceiling too (min of catalog and maxPerRequest), or document that maxPerRequest no longer caps catalog models. Since ImageRegistryConfig can't distinguish explicit vs default... actually it can: default ctor uses `defaultMaxImagesPerRequest`; if user sets it, parseImagesSection returns a config with maxPerRequest set. But `ImageRegistryConfig()` default also has maxPerRequest = 20. Hosts publish `parseImagesSection(...) ?? const ImageRegistryConfig()` — indistinguishable. The clean fix: make maxPerRequest nullable internally (null = default) and resolve `min` where both present. That's a design change; as a reviewer I'll raise it as IMPORTANT and let the author decide.

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1768
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1768
- **Title**: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1750-image-caps` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +858
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:02:57Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T23:27:34Z

## PR Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 — cap N applies, current-first-then-newest drops + notices | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC1: a model with a perModel cap rides ≤ cap uniques") + existing drop-order suite |
| AC2 — resolution order perModel > catalog > default, all combos | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC2: resolution matrix") |
| AC3 — 400 parsed → (modelId, cap) → exactly ONE re-send ≤ learned cap | IT-1 `image_cap_loop_test.dart` (fake provider 400→200; latch map + 2 drops + learned-cap notice asserted) |
| AC4 — second refusal surfaces, turn ends as today | IT-2 (calls == 2, terminal error stop) |
| AC5 — non-matching 400/5xx never re-sends | IT-3 (near-miss `maximum allowed … is 10` without `too many images`, 500, 429 → calls == 1) + UT `image_overflow_test.dart` negatives |
| AC6 — `images.registry: false` byte-identical, no recovery | IT-4 (raw images ride, no latch, no re-send) |
| AC7 — strict perModel validation | UT `config_service_test.dart` (valid/non-int/negative/non-map) |
| E2 — (provider, model)-keyed latch | IT-5 + UT `imageCapLatchKey` |
| E3 — learned cap < 1: no re-send | IT-6 + detector UT |
| E5 — re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry | IT-7 (image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send) |
| REG-1 — legacy shape guard | REG-1 test (no config/catalog: 12 uniques ride, no notices) + existing #171 legacy fixtures untouched |

## Gates (run locally, standalone SDK in-worktree)

- `dart analyze` — full `lib/src` + all touched/new test files: **no issues**
- `dart format` — all 20 touched files formatted with the SDK
- `dart test` (targeted): `test/image_overflow_test.dart` (6), `test/agent/image_registry_test.dart` (25), `test/agent/image_cap_loop_test.dart` (11), `test/config/config_service_test.dart` + `test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_test.dart` — **all pass** (whole-`lib/src` analyze compensates for the no-whole-suite rule)

## Non-goals honored

No send-once/labeling/renumbering changes (#171/#195), no cap raising, no cap persistence (second tier), no video/audio caps, only the measured Google shape in the regex table.

The branch predates main's gh-1757 merge (#1764, `823395d`) and both sides append to the `## Unreleased` section, so the merge is broken. Verified against live `origin/main`:

$ git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in CHANGELOG.md   (exit 1)

The factory bot flagged the same conflict. Please rebase onto `main` and keep both entries under `## Unreleased` (main's entries read newest-first, so `feat(#1750)` slots in below `- fix(gh-1757)`). Validation re-runs automatically after the push.

`_wireImageCapLearnedNotice()` is wired in the CLI only (`agent_cli_io.dart`). Tests look reasonable. Note the AC2 matrix: "perModel absent, catalog present → 10" — the catalog-over-global-default precedence is asserted intentionally. The question of a USER-SET maxPerRequest being overridden by the catalog remains: in the matrix they set `imageRegistryConfig = ImageRegistryConfig(maxPerRequest: 20)` (the default, not user-set) and `resolve(modelId: 'm', catalog: 10)` → 10. So the design intentionally puts catalog above the global default. But when the USER explicitly sets `maxPerRequest: 3`, the catalog still overrides it to 10. There's no way to distinguish "user-set" from "default 20" in the current ImageRegistryConfig (both are just `maxPerRequest: 3` vs default). So user's explicit global cap IS overridden by catalog for catalog models. That's the finding. Severity: the default is 20 and catalog values are measured provider ceilings; the only case where it bites is a user lowering maxPerRequest for token/cost reasons. It contradicts the PR's own "user truth beats built-ins" claim (stated for perModel). I'll flag as IMPORTANT.

Hmm, wait. Let me re-read the PR description: "`images.perModel.<modelId>` config override — ... User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-seter only." And the ImageRegistryConfig.perModel doc: "user truth beats the catalog and the global default". So the author DID think about precedence: perModel (user, per-model) > catalog (built-in, per-model) > maxPerRequest (user global default... or built-in default). The precedence treats maxPerRequest as the lowest layer. Arguably `maxPerRequest` is a GLOBAL default while catalog maxImages is MODEL-SPECIFIC knowledge — more specific wins. That's a defensible reading: model-specific > global. But it's still a silent behavior change for users who set maxPerRequest explicitly for budget reasons: with a catalog model their cap goes UP without notice. Pre-PR, cap was maxPerRequest always.

Practical risk: low-medium. A user who set maxPerRequest: 3 to save tokens now sends 10 images to gemini-4-argon — more cost. No refusal (10 ≤ real cap). It's a real, silent precedence surprise worth an IMPORTANT. I'll phrase it as a question-grade IMPORTANT with a concrete fix: honor an explicitly-configured maxPerRequest as a hard ceiling too (min of catalog and maxPerRequest), or document that maxPerRequest no longer caps catalog models. Since ImageRegistryConfig can't distinguish explicit vs default... actually it can: default ctor uses `defaultMaxImagesPerRequest`; if user sets it, parseImagesSection returns a config with maxPerRequest set. But `ImageRegistryConfig()` default also has maxPerRequest = 20. Hosts publish `parseImagesSection(...) ?? const ImageRegistryConfig()` — indistinguishable. The clean fix: make maxPerRequest nullable internally (null = default) and resolve `min` where both present. That's a design change; as a reviewer I'll raise it as IMPORTANT and let the author decide.

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3.
