# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1768
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1768
- **Title**: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1750-image-caps` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +858
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:02:57Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T23:27:34Z

## PR Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 — cap N applies, current-first-then-newest drops + notices | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC1: a model with a perModel cap rides ≤ cap uniques") + existing drop-order suite |
| AC2 — resolution order perModel > catalog > default, all combos | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC2: resolution matrix") |
| AC3 — 400 parsed → (modelId, cap) → exactly ONE re-send ≤ learned cap | IT-1 `image_cap_loop_test.dart` (fake provider 400→200; latch map + 2 drops + learned-cap notice asserted) |
| AC4 — second refusal surfaces, turn ends as today | IT-2 (calls == 2, terminal error stop) |
| AC5 — non-matching 400/5xx never re-sends | IT-3 (near-miss `maximum allowed … is 10` without `too many images`, 500, 429 → calls == 1) + UT `image_overflow_test.dart` negatives |
| AC6 — `images.registry: false` byte-identical, no recovery | IT-4 (raw images ride, no latch, no re-send) |
| AC7 — strict perModel validation | UT `config_service_test.dart` (valid/non-int/negative/non-map) |
| E2 — (provider, model)-keyed latch | IT-5 + UT `imageCapLatchKey` |
| E3 — learned cap < 1: no re-send | IT-6 + detector UT |
| E5 — re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry | IT-7 (image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send) |
| REG-1 — legacy shape guard | REG-1 test (no config/catalog: 12 uniques ride, no notices) + existing #171 legacy fixtures untouched |

## Gates (run locally, standalone SDK in-worktree)

- `dart analyze` — full `lib/src` + all touched/new test files: **no issues**
- `dart format` — all 20 touched files formatted with the SDK
- `dart test` (targeted): `test/image_overflow_test.dart` (6), `test/agent/image_registry_test.dart` (25), `test/agent/image_cap_loop_test.dart` (11), `test/config/config_service_test.dart` + `test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_test.dart` — **all pass** (whole-`lib/src` analyze compensates for the no-whole-suite rule)

## Non-goals honored

No send-once/labeling/renumbering changes (#171/#195), no cap raising, no cap persistence (second tier), no video/audio caps, only the measured Google shape in the regex table.

There's no way to distinguish "user-set" from "default 20" in the current ImageRegistryConfig (both are just `maxPerRequest: 3` vs default). So user's explicit global cap IS overridden by catalog for catalog models. That's the finding. Severity: the default is 20 and catalog values are measured provider ceilings; the only case where it bites is a user lowering maxPerRequest for token/cost reasons. blocks.text:
# pr-1768: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget

## Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 — cap N applies, current-first-then-newest drops + notices | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC1: a model with a perModel cap rides ≤ cap uniques") + existing drop-order suite |
| AC2 — resolution order perModel > catalog > default, all combos | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC2: resolution matrix") |

blocks.text:
# pr-1768: feat(#1750): per-model image caps — outbound never exceeds the target model's unique-image budget

## Description

Closes #1750

Per-model image caps: the outbound provider request never carries more unique images than the target model accepts, and an image-count 400 degrades by re-sending with fewer images instead of killing the turn.

## Implementation

- **`Model.maxImages`** (`model.dart`): optional per-model unique-image cap alongside `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`. Catalog seed (`provider_catalog.dart`): `gemini-4-argon: 10` (measured, the only pinned value). Wired through every model rebuild path (`buildCatalogModel`, `buildCliDefaultModel`, `/model` switch, endpoint-detected rebuilds, Copilot base-URL rebind, CodeMie paths) so a switch never drops the cap.
- **`images.perModel.<modelId>`** config override — strict `images:` section (`cli_config.dart` parse + `config_service.dart` boot validator; non-int/negative value = `ConfigException` naming the key). User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-setter only.
- **Cap resolution seam** (`resolveImageCap` in `image_registry.dart`): `perModel config > catalog maxImages > images.maxPerRequest` — first present wins, the issue-#1554 scoped-timeout shape.
- **`image_overflow.dart`**: pure refusal classifier next to the context-overflow detector — the pinned Google shape `too many images … maximum allowed for model <id> is <n>` → `(modelId, learnedCap)`; near-misses (cap text without `too many images`) never match.
- **Adaptive latch + one re-send** (agent loop, mirroring the gh-1680 message-cap heal): the learned cap latches per `(provider, model)` pair for the run (runtime-only, never persisted; a `/model` switch never sees another pair's latch), the loop re-sends exactly ONCE — the retry rebuilds fresh through the registry at the smaller cap — and the existing current-first-then-newest cap-drop notices fire (plus a learned-cap notice naming the model and cap; CLI renders a dim line + fa.log entry). A second refusal surfaces the error exactly as today.

## Invariants

- Session JSONL is never rewritten (payload-only rewrites throughout).
- `images.registry: false`: no cap logic, no re-send, byte-identical legacy request shape including this recovery.
- Models with no catalog entry and an undocumented limit that never errors in the pinned shape → first refusal surfaces raw (honest degradation).
- Degenerate learned cap (`is 0`) classifies as the family but never re-sends.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 — cap N applies, current-first-then-newest drops + notices | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC1: a model with a perModel cap rides ≤ cap uniques") + existing drop-order suite |
| AC2 — resolution order perModel > catalog > default, all combos | UT `image_registry_test.dart` ("AC2: resolution matrix") |
| AC3 — 400 parsed → (modelId, cap) → exactly ONE re-send ≤ learned cap | IT-1 `image_cap_loop_test.dart` (fake provider 400→200; latch map + 2 drops + learned-cap notice asserted) |
| AC4 — second refusal surfaces, turn ends as today | IT-2 (calls == 2, terminal error stop) |
| AC5 — non-matching 400/5xx never re-sends | IT-3 (near-miss `maximum allowed … is 10` without `too many images`, 500, 429 → calls == 1) + UT `image_overflow_test.dart` negatives |
| AC6 — `images.registry: false` byte-identical, no recovery | IT-4 (raw images ride, no latch, no re-send) |
| AC7 — strict perModel validation | UT `config_service_test.dart` (valid/non-int/negative/non-map) |
| E2 — (provider, model)-keyed latch | IT-5 + UT `imageCapLatchKey` |
| E3 — learned cap < 1: no re-send | IT-6 + detector UT |
| E5 — re-send rebuilds fresh through the registry | IT-7 (image arriving between send and re-send rides the capped re-send) |
| REG-1 — legacy shape guard | REG-1 test (no config/catalog: 12 uniques ride, no notices) + existing #171 legacy fixtures untouched |

## Gates (run locally, standalone SDK in-worktree)

- `dart analyze` — full `lib/src` + all touched/new test files: **no issues**
- `dart format` — all 20 touched files formatted with the SDK
- `dart test` (targeted): `test/image_overflow_test.dart` (6), `test/agent/image_registry_test.dart` (25), `test/agent/image_cap_loop_test.dart` (11), `test/config/config_service_test.dart` + `test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart` + `test/agent/agent_test.dart` — **all pass** (whole-`lib/src` analyze compensates for the no-whole-suite rule)

## Non-goals honored

No send-once/labeling/renumbering changes (#171/#195), no cap raising, no cap persistence (second tier), no video/audio caps, only the measured Google shape in the regex table.

Tests look reasonable. Note the AC2 matrix: "perModel absent, catalog present → 10" — the catalog-over-global-default precedence is asserted intentionally. The question of a USER-SET maxPerRequest being overridden by the catalog remains: in the matrix they set `imageRegistryConfig = ImageRegistryConfig(maxPerRequest: 20)` (the default, not user-set) and `resolve(modelId: 'm', catalog: 10)` → 10. So the design intentionally puts catalog above the global default. But when the USER explicitly sets `maxPerRequest: 3`, the catalog still overrides it to 10. There's no way to distinguish "user-set" from "default 20" in the current ImageRegistryConfig (both are just `maxPerRequest: 3` vs default). So user's explicit global cap IS overridden by catalog for catalog models. That's the finding. Severity: the default is 20 and catalog values are measured provider ceilings; the only case where it bites is a user lowering maxPerRequest for token/cost reasons. It contradicts the PR's own "user truth beats built-ins" claim (stated for perModel). I'll flag as IMPORTANT.

Hmm, wait. Let me re-read the PR description: "`images.perModel.<modelId>` config override — ... User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-seter only." And the ImageRegistryConfig.perModel doc: "user truth beats the catalog and the global default". So the author DID think about precedence: perModel (user, per-model) > catalog (built-in, per-model) > maxPerRequest (user global default... or built-in default). The precedence treats maxPerRequest as the lowest layer. Arguably `maxPerRequest` is a GLOBAL default while catalog maxImages is MODEL-SPECIFIC knowledge — more specific wins. That's a defensible reading: model-specific > global. But it's still a silent behavior change for users who set maxPerRequest explicitly for budget reasons: with a catalog model their cap goes UP without notice. Pre-PR, cap was maxPerRequest always.

Practical risk: low-medium. A user who set maxPerRequest: 3 to save tokens now sends 10 images to gemini-4-argon — more cost. No refusal (10 ≤ real cap). It's a real, silent precedence surprise worth an IMPORTANT. I'll phrase it as a question-grade IMPORTANT with a concrete fix: honor an explicitly-configured maxPerRequest as a hard ceiling too (min of catalog and maxPerRequest), or document that maxPerRequest no longer caps catalog models. Since ImageRegistryConfig can't distinguish explicit vs default... actually it can: default ctor uses `defaultMaxImagesPerRequest`; if user sets it, parseImagesSection returns a config with maxPerRequest set. But `ImageRegistryConfig()` default also has maxPerRequest = 20. Hosts publish `parseImagesSection(...) ?? const ImageRegistryConfig()` — indistinguishable. The clean fix: make maxPerRequest nullable internally (null = default) and resolve `min` where both present. That's a design change; as a reviewer I'll raise it as IMPORTANT and let the author decide.

return catalogMaxImages == null ? global : math.min(catalogMaxImages, global);

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `int.parse` can throw on provider-controlled text — breaking the classifier's "returns null for everything else" contract**

`learnedCap: int.parse(match.group(2)!)` — the captured group is `(\d+)` with no length bound, and `errorMessage` is arbitrary provider-controlled text: `classifyImageCapError` runs on **every** error stop via `_needsImageCapHeal`. A buggy or hostile endpoint answering the pinned shape with a >64-bit digit run (`… too many images: maximum allowed for model m is 999…`) makes `int.parse` throw `FormatException` inside `healIfNeeded` → `_finishedTurnResult` → `_streamAttempt`, and the retry loop in `_streamAssistantResponse` has no try/catch — the turn dies on an internal exception instead of surfacing the provider error.

The twin parser in this very directory already handles the same trust surface correctly — `overflow.dart:197` uses `int.tryParse`. Suggested fix:

```dart
final cap = int.tryParse(match.group(2)!);
if (cap == null) continue; // unparseable cap ≡ not the refusal family
return ImageCapRefusal(modelId: match.group(1)!, learnedCap: cap);
```

One line, and the doc contract ("Returns null for everything else") becomes actually true.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the app host never sees the learned-cap notice** *(carried over from round 1 — still open after the rebase push; the rework touched only the CHANGELOG)*

`_wireImageCapLearnedNotice()` is wired in the CLI only (`agent_cli_io.dart`). The Flutter app wires every other "never silent" notice through `AppLog.i` — `_wireImageDropNotice` (F4), `_wireOperativePinNotice` (gh-1409), the text-only drops (#638) in `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart` — but nothing sets `imageCapLearnedNotice` there. In the desktop app an adaptive re-send therefore logs the per-image drop lines with no "provider refused / cap learned" context line, which is exactly the confusion the notice exists to prevent.

Mirror the pattern in `AgentService` (an `AppLog.i('images', 'provider refused: too many images for $modelId — cap learned: $cap; re-sending with fewer images')` from a `_wireImageCapLearnedNotice` next to `_wireImageDropNotice`) so both hosts tell the same story.

💡 **SUGGESTION: provider-controlled text interpolated into the terminal line** *(carried over from round 1 — still open)*

`modelId` here is regex-extracted from the raw provider error body (`classifyImageCapError`, group `(.+?)`) — a buggy or hostile endpoint can embed ANSI escape sequences or control characters that ride verbatim into this `io.writeln` and scramble the transcript. The same trust surface already exists for `errorMessage` rendering, so this is hardening, not a new hole: consider stripping control chars from `refusal.modelId` (e.g. `replaceAll(RegExp(r'[\x00-\x1f\x7f]'), '')`) before interpolation — one line, and the fa.log entry benefits too.

💡 **SUGGESTION: perModel validation now lives in two hand-synced copies** *(carried over from round 1 — still open)*

The strict rules (must be a `YamlMap`; every value a positive `int` naming the offending key) are implemented twice — here in the boot validator and again in `parseImagesSection`'s `readPerModelCap`/`readPerModel` (`cli_config.dart`). This extends the pre-existing `maxPerRequest` duplication, so it follows the local pattern, but the two copies must now drift in lockstep (messages are asserted by tests on both sides). When the third `images:` key arrives, consider extracting one shared validator both paths call so the strict schema has a single source of truth.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `agent_loop.dart` is at 97.6% of the 2800-line loc gate** *(carried over from round 1 — unchanged, 2733/2800)*

Tests look reasonable. Note the AC2 matrix: "perModel absent, catalog present → 10" — the catalog-over-global-default precedence is asserted intentionally. The question of a USER-SET maxPerRequest being overridden by the catalog remains: in the matrix they set `imageRegistryConfig = ImageRegistryConfig(maxPerRequest: 20)` (the default, not user-set) and `resolve(modelId: 'm', catalog: 10)` → 10. So the design intentionally puts catalog above the global default. But when the USER explicitly sets `maxPerRequest: 3`, the catalog still overrides it to 10. There's no way to distinguish "user-set" from "default 20" in the current ImageRegistryConfig (both are just `maxPerRequest: 3` vs default). So user's explicit global cap IS overridden by catalog for catalog models. That's the finding. Severity: the default is 20 and catalog values are measured provider ceilings; the only case where it bites is a user lowering maxPerRequest for token/cost reasons. It contradicts the PR's own "user truth beats built-ins" claim (stated for perModel). I'll flag as IMPORTANT.

Hmm, wait. Let me re-read the PR description: "`images.perModel.<modelId>` config override — ... User truth beats built-ins; ceiling-seter only." And the ImageRegistryConfig.perModel doc: "user truth beats the catalog and the global default". So the author DID think about precedence: perModel (user, per-model) > catalog (built-in, per-model) > maxPerRequest (user global default... or built-in default). The precedence treats maxPerRequest as the lowest layer. Arguably `maxPerRequest` is a GLOBAL default while catalog maxImages is MODEL-SPECIFIC knowledge — more specific wins. That's a defensible reading: model-specific > global. But it's still a silent behavior change for users who set maxPerRequest explicitly for budget reasons: with a catalog model their cap goes UP without notice. Pre-PR, cap was maxPerRequest always.

Practical risk: low-medium. A user who set maxPerRequest: 3 to save tokens now sends 10 images to gemini-4-argon — more cost. No refusal (10 ≤ real cap). It's a real, silent precedence surprise worth an IMPORTANT. I'll phrase it as a question-grade IMPORTANT with a concrete fix: honor an explicitly-configured maxPerRequest as a hard ceiling too (min of catalog and maxPerRequest), or document that maxPerRequest no longer caps catalog models. Since ImageRegistryConfig can't distinguish explicit vs default... actually it can: default ctor uses `defaultMaxImagesPerRequest`; if user sets it, parseImagesSection returns a config with maxPerRequest set. But `ImageRegistryConfig()` default also has maxPerRequest = 20. Hosts publish `parseImagesSection(...) ?? const ImageRegistryConfig()` — indistinguishable. The clean fix: make maxPerRequest nullable internally (null = default) and resolve `min` where both present. That's a design change; as a reviewer I'll raise it as IMPORTANT and let the author decide.
